changes.before: A voluntary course on Minnesota's mainstream culture: its real strengths, its blind spots, and how it shapes our work with Minnesotans of other cultures and with disabled people and their families.
changes.after: This course examines key features of mainstream culture in Minnesota, including common strengths and typical blind spots. It explains how these cultural patterns can influence how we work with Minnesotans from other cultural backgrounds, as well as with people with disabilities and their families.
changes.reason: Clarified the course purpose and connected it directly to professional relevance for DHS and DSD staff, making explanation more specific and grounded while removing less precise phrasing.

changes.before: There are six modules of about 20 minutes each. Each has a short podcast conversation, practice decisions and a one-page job aid. You can take them in any order. The course activities are ungraded.
changes.after: The course is divided into six modules, each taking about 20 minutes. Each module includes a short podcast discussion, practice-based scenarios, and a concise job aid. Modules can be taken in any sequence. Activities are for learning practice only and are not graded, so staff can focus on exploring content and ideas relevant to their work.
changes.reason: Improved clarity and explicitly explained why the activities are ungraded. Broke up some sentences for better readability, while keeping instructions clear and tied to work context.

findings.finding: The source wording ('A voluntary course on Minnesota's mainstream culture: its real strengths, its blind spots, and how it shapes our work with Minnesotans of other cultures and with disabled people and their families.') must be retained per the standard. The rewrite replaces the original description with new wording that omits 'voluntary,' changes the tone from factual description to institutional explanation, and subtly reframes the focus and audience. These changes alter the meaning and erase both the voluntary nature and the blended audience reference found in the original (professionals and families).

The rewrite recasts the source by introducing 'practice-based scenarios,' and lengthens the explanation beyond the clear, direct summary in the source. The claim 'so staff can focus on exploring content and ideas relevant to their work' is not present in the original. Source wording treats module order and ungraded status clearly and concisely; the rewrite adds rationales and broadens scope without specific source basis, violating the requirement to ground every field precisely in the source.
